newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products- Group 3 gasoline diffs widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products- Group 3 gasoline diffs widen.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products edged higher with NYMEX, with differentials little changed except for a firming of conventional unleaded gasoline in the Group 3 midcontinent market.
NYMEX heating oil rose about 0.36 cent a gallon to 51.80 cents by early afternoon, while NYMEX gasoline gained 0.22 cent to 57.00 cents.

Group Three prompt unleaded gasoline differentials rose Thursday amid a spate of short-covering and fairly low supply levels. Players said there were about 18 days of supply, or 5.2 million barrels, of gasoline recorded in the Williams Pipeline system as of today, which is considered the low end of the range.
This morning prompt conventional unleaded traded as high as 4.80 cents over July NYMEX, about 0.75 cent above Wednesday differentials. Any-month also strengthened to 3.60/3.80 cents.
"People are looking to cover," said one trader, noting the slight rise in NYMEX futures.
Chicago market unleaded gasoline was pegged mostly steady, with prompt third cycle at 1.10/1.25 cents over the print. Prompt July was considered even.
Traders said NYH heating oil was offered at about 0.25 cent below July futures, stable with Wednesday differentials, with the Sun Co posting a price of 0.30 cent under the screen earlier in the day.

"People are putting heat away for winter storage. Over the past few days, at least several hundred thousand barrels have traded hands," one New York trader said, adding it was brisk activity for this time of year.
"Last summer you couldn't give it away in the harbor. But NYMEX is in contango now, so people can afford to put it in tank and sell January" barrels, he said.
NYH conventional unleaded "M2" gasoline was offered at about 2.75 cents below July futures, stable with Wednesday diffs, traders said.
Premium 93-octane "V2" sold for 4.50 cents over the screen, while reformulated 93-octane "D2" was traded for 7.50 cents over, players added.

Differentials continued their recent pattern of stability on most USG products, with activity described on the light side. Prompt USG heating oil sold for 2.25 cents below the July print, with low sulfur diesel also steady with offers at 1.60 cent below the screen, traders said.
Aviation-quality 54-grade jet fuel was sold for 0.25 cent over the screen, also stable.
Diffs on USG conventional unleaded "M1" grade gasoline, meanwhile, held pat with offers at 3.50 cents below July futures, traders said.
(( - Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk 212 859-1620))
